screen: quotes — all 8 screens (quotations list + detail, clients, catalog, invoices list + detail, reports, settings)
macrostructure: Workbench (quotations, clients, invoices) · Ledger (catalog, and nested in every detail pane) · Stacked Sections (reports, settings)
differs_from: first recorded run for this app — no prior entry to diversify against. The Command Deck attractor was rejected explicitly: the job here is working a record to a decision, not monitoring at a glance. The three summary figures that would have been its KPI cards are a single ruled Position strip instead, and on a phone they are reordered BELOW the list.

exceptions.rule: A list or table with no overflow behaviour: no pagination, no virtualisation, no stated cap.
exceptions.why: GET /quotations returns every row and the rail renders all of them. At the fixture's 8 records and the business's real volume this is correct and fast, but there is no cap, no page and no virtual window, so the gate fails honestly rather than being argued away. Filed as a todo.
exceptions.would_close_it: Either a stated cap surfaced in .rail-count ('showing first 200 of N') or a real page/scroll window in workbench.js. The API already supports the query shape; the UI does not use it.

exceptions.rule: Row height above 48px in a Ledger or Feed.
exceptions.status: accepted — in direct conflict with A4
exceptions.why: The catalog Ledger measures a 62px median row at 1440. That is arithmetic, not sloppiness: the row carries three inline controls, and a 36px control inside 8px+8px cell padding and a 1px rule is 61px. Raising those controls to A4's 44px would make the row 69px; shrinking the row under 48px would put the controls under 32px. N2 and A4 cannot both hold for a row with inline actions, and this build resolved it toward the target size.
exceptions.would_close_it: Moving Edit/Delete out of the row — a hover-revealed action column or an overflow menu — which trades a visible affordance for a hidden one. Not obviously the better screen; recorded rather than done.

exceptions.why: Every primary control is 44px. The exceptions are button.sm (36px) on catalog rows and inline line-edit rows, and the rail-head search/filter (40px), all of which exist to keep the density floors the same rubric demands in N1-N3. WCAG 2.2 AA (2.5.8) requires 24x24; 44x44 is 2.5.5, which is AAA. Measured minimum across all 8 screens is 36px, comfortably above the AA floor, and the harness reports the AA and AAA counts separately so this can never be mistaken for a pass.
exceptions.would_close_it: A density mode switch — 44px targets in a 'comfortable' setting, current sizes in 'compact'. Worth doing if an operator ever asks; nobody has.

critique.note: Specificity is a 4 rather than a 5 because a Workbench is a well-known shape; what another model would not have produced from this brief is the status encoding that survives greyscale (colour AND border style on the rail's left edge), the delete rule keyed to invoice existence rather than to status, and the Position strip demoted below the records on a phone.

measured.notes: light_browser verb:eval is unavailable in this environment, so the measurement runs in-page and is read back as a text snapshot. Chrome CORS-blocks ES module imports from file://, which is why the harness is an HTTP server rather than a file:// open — it also means every measurement exercises the real API transport.
